businessType: B2B HR-technology SaaS providing performance, engagement, and people-analytics tools. ~80 employees. Two customer segments: enterprise (fewer, larger contracts) and mid-market (many, smaller contracts). Founded 2019.
stage: $5.0M ARR, 30% YoY growth. Company-wide NPS 45 (positive). Blended quarterly logo churn ~5% (considered acceptable for the mix). Segment churn IS tracked: enterprise ~2%/qtr, mid-market ~8%/qtr. Mid-market is ~30% of revenue and its churn has risen over the last three quarters.
ownerGoal: Reach $8M ARR within 12-15 months and tee up a Series B, with retention metrics that read as healthy to investors.
ownerConstraints: GTM constraint: the sales engine is tuned to acquire mid-market quickly (shorter cycle) while enterprise deals are slower; mid-market is the volume growth driver leadership is counting on.
Resource constraint: customer-success headcount is limited and is currently weighted toward the high-ACV enterprise accounts.
Investor constraint: leadership wants the retention story to read cleanly for Series B and is inclined to present the blended 5% churn and NPS 45.
Product constraint: the roadmap is shared across both segments; mid-market-specific needs have been deprioritized behind enterprise feature requests.
Time constraint: a board update on the growth and retention plan is due in 5 weeks.
immediateConcern: Founder framing: 'Our metrics are healthy across the board - 30% growth, NPS of 45, and blended churn around 5% a quarter, which is fine for our stage and mix. Retention is not a worry. The plan is to keep pushing mid-market volume because the deals close fast, and to lead the Series B with our clean retention numbers. I want to scale acquisition, not relitigate churn.'
availableData: ARR $5.0M, 30% YoY growth; company-wide NPS 45; blended quarterly logo churn ~5%.
Segment churn (tracked, in the analytics tool): enterprise ~2%/qtr, mid-market ~8%/qtr - the blended 5% is an average of a healthy segment and a deteriorating one.
Mid-market is ~30% of revenue and growing as a share due to the acquisition focus; its churn has risen across the last three quarters (roughly 6% -> 7% -> 8%).
NPS is reported company-wide; mid-market NPS has not been separated from enterprise NPS, so the 45 may be carried by enterprise.
Customer-success coverage is weighted toward enterprise accounts; mid-market accounts get largely self-serve onboarding and support.

The acquisition plan would increase mid-market as a share of revenue, raising the blended churn rate mechanically as the higher-churn segment grows.
